segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
Shirkuh [became] vizier in his place,
and he was also called 'king' and 'commander-in-chief',
for so were the viziers of Egypt called.
And when this Shirkuh had lived for only two months in his vizierate,
he died of a disease of strangulation (quinsy).
And in his place arose his brother's son, Saladin, son of Najm al-Din Ayyub.
And by the abundance of his gifts,
he made all the armies his friends,
and gained dominion over Egypt.
And to Asad al-Din Shirkuh one son remained whose name was Nasir al-Din,
to whom and to whose sons Homs belonged.
And to Najm al-Din Ayyub his brother there were six sons:
The first,
Shams al-Dawla Turan Shah,
who ruled over Alexandria.
The second,
Shahinshah, the father of 'Izz al-Din Farrukh Shah
and of Taqi al-Din 'Umar,
to whom and to whose sons Hama belonged.
The third,
Sayf al-Islam Tughtekin,
who ruled over the South (Yemen).
The fourth,
Saladin Yusuf,
who reigned over Egypt, Palestine, Syria, and Mesopotamia.
The fifth,
Malik 'Adil Abu Bakr,
who arose after Saladin.
The sixth,
Taj al-Muluk Buri (Turi?):
who died while Saladin was encamped against Aleppo.
And in the year 1481
[1481 of the Greeks?],
Muhammad, the ruler of Melitene,
having become detested by the nobles and the citizens,
because he was attached to an adulterous, sorceress woman,
took the adulteress and sorceress and went out from Melitene,
and went wandering about from place to place.
And the nobles and the citizens set up in his place Abu'l-Qasim, his younger brother.
And the king of Jerusalem,
when he heard of the evils which Mleh the Armenian, ruler of Cilicia, was inflicting upon the Christians,
was moved with zeal and went against him, and shut him up in a certain fortress.
And when Mleh was hard-pressed,
he offered repentance,
and swore that he would be in subjection to the king,
and would not ally himself with the Turks.
And then he left him and went away.
And in the same year,
which is 565,
[565 of the Arabs?, died Qutb al-Din Mawdud, son of Zengi, lord] of Mosul.
And he commanded that his son 'Imad al-Din Zengi, son of Mawdud, son of Zengi, should succeed in his place.
And this Qutb al-Din had a deputy and administrator of his kingdom who was called Fakhr al-Din 'Abd al-Masih,
[Page] 338
